text:
ana: heads-up — found a quirky interop bug in the retriever+rerank sampleapp when using Go and Ruby SDKs together. batching helper + auth refresh = missing vector + dim flip + inconsistent rerank shape.

chris: interesting. we tend to see node/python, not go/ruby. can you paste minimal repro and what you expect?

ana: repro: 10 docs, batchingHelper batch_size=4, use Go SDK to produce corpus embeddings and Ruby SDK to call rerank. Force auth token rotation mid-first-subbatch. expected: 10 embeddings in doc order and rerank returns `{scores: [...]}`. observed: Go client returns 9 embeddings, one duped, vector dim 384; Ruby rerank call sometimes gets top-level flat array of floats instead of `{scores}`. also rerank ranking mismatches because sizes off.

patrick: that sounds like three linked issues: (1) retry + mutable batch queue -> missing/duplicate, (2) routing/fallback variant changed dim, (3) SDK shape parity for rerank responses. logs?

ana: logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-08-01T08:22:11Z] batching: snapshot batch0 ids=[0,1,2,3]
[2026-08-01T08:22:11Z] auth: refresh start (TTL rotated)
[2026-08-01T08:22:11Z] embeddings-go: send batch0 (snapshot) size=4
[2026-08-01T08:22:12Z] embeddings-go: 401 -> retrying (snapshot present)
[2026-08-01T08:22:12Z] embeddings-go: send batch0 (retry) size=3 // server responded with 3 vectors
[2026-08-01T08:22:12Z] embeddings-go: vec_dim=384 model_alias=redwood-open-lite
[2026-08-01T08:22:13Z] rerank-ruby: received scores as array length=9 not object
[2026-08-01T08:22:13Z] final: merged_embeddings=9 expected=10
```

chris: size=3 is surprising. server should return same length as inputs or fail. the vec_dim=384 suggests retry hit a low-dim fallback. we route retries to cheaper variants under load, which is intended, but we didn't enforce output-dim contract.

patrick: Go helper passed a snapshot but why size=3? maybe server-side partial success for one of the inputs on retry. we need server to either return 4 vectors or an explicit per-input error. client-side merging by position will break if partials occur.

ana: repro code (Go):
```go
items := make([]Item, len(docs))
for i,d := range docs { items[i] = Item{ID:i, Text:d} }
err := batchingHelper.Enqueue(items, func(sub []Item) ([]float32, error) {
  texts := make([]string, len(sub))
  for i,s := range sub { texts[i] = s.Text }
  resp, err := client.Embeddings(context.Background(), EmbeddingRequest{Input: texts})
  return resp.Vectors, err
})
```

patrick: few pragmatic fixes: (A) require snapshot with explicit ids+payloads and treat server response as position-mapped to snapshot ids (client already does this but make it enforced); (B) server must return errors for inputs it couldn't process instead of silently returning fewer vectors; (C) SDKs (Go/Ruby) normalize rerank/embeddings shapes: always return `{embeddings: [...], model: "alias"}` and `{scores: [...], model: "alias"}`; (D) model-catalog contract: all variants for alias must have same output_dim or router must stick to same variant on retries.

chris: short-term we can: implement (A) in the Go batching helper (snapshot and merge by id), add a shim in Ruby to normalize rerank responses, and add an input-validation check: if server returns N != snapshot_len, throw an error and log full response (fail-fast) so sampleapps surface the issue.

ana: I pushed a Go PR that snapshots sub-batches and merges by id: https://github.com/redwoodinc/redwood-sdk-go/pull/412 — local runs stopped the missing/dup symptom. opened a Ruby PR for response normalization: https://github.com/redwoodinc/redwood-sdk-ruby/pull/98.

patrick: add tests: unit test that injects 401 mid-flight and asserts merged length == original, and an e2e that rotates tokens in canary infra hitting router fallbacks. also add a server-side check to reject mixed-dim batches with a 409 and a helpful message.

dev-ci-bot: canary build queued for branch ana/batch-go-snapshot (build 5012).

ruby-sdk-bot: noted. will add a compatibility shim for previous users expecting flat arrays. will deprecate old shape in next minor.

chris: docs action items: add "Cross-SDK embedding parity" note in onboarding, document `model_alias` contract, and add a troubleshooting flowchart: missing vector -> check batching helper snapshot -> check server partial response -> check routing/model alias.

ana: one more quirky thing — rerank Ruby returned a flat array only when the call came from a background job (sidekiq) and not from web request. might be environment-related serialization quirk; investigating.

patrick: ok let's prioritize: 1) enforce client-side snapshot+merge by id (ana's PR), 2) fail-fast on mismatched lengths, 3) SDK normalization shim, 4) model-catalog contract RFC. assign owners and ship.

ana: owner assigned to me for client fixes, pat for server contract RFC. thanks all :zap:
